author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read F5 BIG-IP ASM (Advanced WAF) security logs, APM access logs and AFM network firewall and DoS logs. ASM, APM and AFM send their logs to the data collector over syslog. ASM requests go to HTTP and violations and attack events to NIDS, APM session messages to Auth, and AFM firewall events to Netflow and DoS events to NIDS.
notes:
Setup:
- ASM / Advanced WAF: give the application security logging profile a remote storage destination (the data collector) in the Key-Value Pairs (Splunk) or Common Event Format (ArcSight) format.
- APM: send access logs to the data collector over remote syslog (RFC 3164).
- AFM: give the network firewall and DoS logging profile a log publisher with a Remote Syslog destination in rfc5424 format, or a Splunk or ArcSight one, to the data collector; rfc3164 and legacy-bigip send fields by position only and aren't read.

Field mapping:
- ASM: requests with no violation go to HTTP (logged only when the profile's request type is all requests); violations, blocked or alerted requests and attack events (brute force, web scraping, DoS) go to NIDS.
- Sophos NG-SIEM's SPLIT_NAME_VALUES cuts a quoted value at a comma, so the ASM parent splits its pairs on tabs it puts between them (Run Test, 2026-10-16: 288 of 288 fields).
- APM: new session, username, policy ending, access policy result, AD authentication failure and session deleted messages go to Auth, each with the session ID; APM splits one logon over several lines, so join them on session_id in search.
- F5 publishes no full APM message catalogue, so only these confirmed messages are read.
- AFM: firewall events (23003137) go to Netflow with addresses, ports, protocol and NAT, Accept, Established, Open and Closed as allowed and Drop and Reject as blocked, and the rule, policy and context in event_metadata.
- AFM: network, DNS and SIP DoS events go to NIDS with the attack name, ID and stage.

Time:
- ASM: times have no zone and are read as UTC.
- AFM: rfc5424 times come from the header; others from date_time or rt, read as UTC.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up from F5's examples and field lists.
- AFM samples follow F5's field tables and examples.

Testing:
- Each ASM child, combined with the parent into one parser, and the APM parser passed Run Test in the lab tenant, and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines.
- On 2026-10-14 each ASM child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under the parent.
- No built-in parser matched the ASM lines.
- On 2026-10-16 in a lab tenant each AFM child passed Run Test flattened (119 of 119 fields in each of 3 runs) and as a separate parser under its parent (9 of 9 lines); no built-in parser claimed AFM lines.

Known gaps:
- ASM: the comma separated format is positional and isn't covered.
- The tenant's built-in F5_LTM parser also matches the APM lines and normalizes nothing; the engine picks one parser per line, and the APM parser took them in 18 of 30 Run Tests on 2026-10-16.
